5. Petitioners' case is that, as per Organisation Order 15 of 1994 six posts of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V were to be filled up from Pay Group IV on promotion on the basis of combined seniority list of Senior Mechanics, Senior Electricians and Senior Bench Fitters, but by the Order previous Organisation Chart has been revised in a manner whereupon Mechanics, Electricians and Bench Fitters who previously used to be promoted its a matter of course to Pay Group V on the basis of combined seniority list, now would be promoted to Pay Group V on the basis of separate seniority list of the said 3 trades circulated under Memo No. DACGE/Seniority list/GSE/95/5946 dated 30-12-95 although promotion from Pay Group V to Pay Group VI and onward would be on the basis of combined seniority list and that would affect petitioners' seniority as an officer of Pay Group V who was junior to them would be supervising officers of all the 3 trades namely, Mechanics, Electricians and Bench Fitters in Pay Group IV. Further case of the petitioners is that, they made representation against distribution of 6 posts of Junior Officers Maintenance by the Order at the ratio 3 : 2 : 1 respectively in 3 trades as the same seriously affected the petitioners as well as the personnel of petitioners' trade and that the order was not legal as the same was violative of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Ordinance, 1977, hereinafter, in short, the Ordinance, and that the said order having not been passed by the Board of Directors of the Corporation but by the Director Administration, and that the seniority list of GSE Department prepared on the basis of the order and issued on 30-12-95 has no legal basis being violative of the Ordinance and Organisation setup that was in existence previous to the making of the Order and that the Order has not been passed in accordance with the Bangladesh Biman Corporation Employees (Service) Regulations 1979, hereinafter, in short, the Regulations, while Organisation Order 15 of 1994 was passed in accordance with the Regulations and Organisation set-up of the Corporation and the same was not violative of petitioners' seniority position. It is also the contention of the petitioners that seniority of Mechanics, Electricians and Bench Fitters of GSE Department in Pay Group V was combined since inception of the Corporation and thus the change in the Organisation set up and the separate seniority list prepared on the basis of the Order are arbitrary and without lawful authority and violative, of fundamental rights guaranteed by Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. 

 6. The Rule was contested by the respondent Nos. 1-4 as well as by the added respondent Nos. 5 and 6 by filing separate affidavits-in-opposition. The contentions of the respondents are almost similar. 

 7. The case of the respondent Nos. 1-4, in short, is that work performed by the three sections are distinct as well as different, as such, as a matter of necessity the provision for maintaining separate seniority of the said 3 categories of employees has been provided for by the Order which is consistent with the last paragraph of Regulation 15 of the Regulations, that the Order and the seniority list circulated by memo dated 30-12-95 are in no way inconsistent with the provision of the Ordinance and Organisation Order 15 of 1994, that to suit the setup in the line of respective trades and that for proper implementation of Organisation Order 15 of 1994, the Order has been issued and 6 posts of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V of GSE Department has been organised in the 3 different trades namely, Mechanic, Electrician and Bench Fitting, as Junior Officer Maintenance and Junior Officer Electrician and Junior Officer Bench Fitting in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1 respectively, that by the order which has been passed legally, the petitioners have not been prejudiced in any way and that in no way and manner seniority of the petitioners have been disturbed by the seniority list issued and circulated  by the memo dated 30-12-1995, nor their promotion would be disturbed, that seniority list issued by memo dated 30-12-1995 is quite legal and the same has been prepared in accordance with law and that said list has not affected the petitioners in any manner as well as in any respect, nor any legal right of the petitioners has been violated, that petitioners being workers within the meaning of Industrial Relations Ordinance, 1969 and that being members of Trade Union they have separate forum for redress' of their grievance, in any respect, that the Corporation as per Regulation 15 of the Regulations maintains separate seniority list of different trade/cadres and, as such, petitioners' claim of combined seniority list of 3 trades viz. Mechanic, Electrician and Bench Fitting, is not sustainable in law Regulation, that the Order has been passed by the competent authority and in passing the same no provision of the Ordinance, or any fundamental right as claimed by petitioners, has been violated, that seniority list issued and circulated under memo dated 30-12-1995 suffers from no illegality as same has been prepared in compliance of last paragraph of Regulation 15 of the Regulations. 

 8. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute on the findings that under Organisation Order 15 of 1994 provision for promotion from Pay Group IV to the Post of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V was on the basis of combined seniority list but Organisation Chart of GSE Department as has been made by the Organisation Order 13 of 1995, the employees of three shops of maintenance cadre who earlier used to be promoted to Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V on the basis of combined seniority list would be promoted to Pay Group V on the basis of separate seniority list of said three shops, that no reason has been offered in Organisation Order 13 of 1995 in the distribution of 6 posts of Junior Officer Maintenance at the ratio 3 : 2 : 1 in the three shops i.e. Mechanic, Electrician and Bench Fitting and that said distribution would deprive the Senior Bench Fitters from being promoted as Junior Officer Maintenance in Pay Group V, that as because of separate Seniority list of Mechanics, Electricians and Bench Fitters issued on making of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 junior personnel of Mechanics are being promoted to Pay Group V in deprivation of petitioners who are admittedly senior and the promotion of the same kind is violation of the provision of Regulations, 1979 as well as fundamental right of the petitioners as guaranteed by Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution and that also discriminatory, that Director Administration by virtue of delegation of authority by the Board of Directors of the Bangladesh Biman Corporation is vested with the power to make Organisation Order 13 of 1995, but as on the basis of the said Organisation Order Separate Seniority List of the three shops has been prepared and circulated and thereby seniority of the petitioners has been adversely affected, the Organisation Order 13 of 1995 and the separate seniority list issued under the memo dated 13-12-1995, so far the same relates to petitioners, are not legal. 

 9. Leave has been granted to consider the contention of the appellants whether High Court Division was in error in finding that under Organisation Order 15 of 1994 a combined seniority of the personnel in Pay Group IV of the Mechanics, Electricians and Bench Fitters of GSE Department was maintained for promotion to Pay Group V, that by Organisation Order 13 of 1995, the Corporation has only fixed the number of posts in Pay Group V of the 3 separate trades on the basis of the requirement of manpower and that separate seniority list of the 3 trades issued under the memo dated 13-12-1995 is not the first time one, as prior to the issuance of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 separate seniority list was in existence, that in view of the Provisions in Regulation 12 and 15 of the Regulations 1979 High Court Division was in error in holding that promotion to Pay Groups V from Pay Group IV to be made on the basis of seniority and on the basis of combined seniority list alone and that petitioners (in Writ Petition) have vested right for promotion. 

 10. The case of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 (petitioners in writ petition) is that prior to making of Organisation Order 15 of 1994 and that after making of the Organisation Order 15 of 1994 there was practice of maintaining combined seniority list of the three shops i.e. Mechanical, Electrical and Bench Fitting in GSE Department and was in operation and that promotion from Pay Group IV to V i.e. to the posts of Junior Officers Maintenance used to be made from amongst the senior most of the said combined seniority list, but by the Organisation Order 13 of 1995 posts of 6 Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V have been distributed at the ratio 3 : 2 : 1 in the three shops of GSE Department as mentioned herein above and that has introduced making of separate seniority list of the said three shops in. canceling maintaining of previously existing combined seniority list and thereby upon depriving petitioners of the secured right of being promoted to Pay Group V persons junior to them have been promoted to Pay Group V. 

 11. As against the aforesaid case of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2, it is the case of appellants, of both the appeals, that at no point of time there was practice of maintaining combined seniority list of the personnel of the aforementioned three shops of the GSE Department and that at no point of time promotion to Pay Group V was made on the basis of combined list as claimed by the respondent Nos. 1 and 2. It is also the case of the appellants that by Organisation Order 13 of 1995 posts of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V has been distributed proportionate to the total number of personnel in the 3 shops of GSE Department i.e. Mechanic, Electrician and Bench Fitter and that it is totally incorrect to say that for, the first time by Organisation Order 13 of 1995 separate list of seniority of the personnel of 3 shops has been introduced and that circulated by the memo dated 30-12-1995. 

 (2) Separate seniority lists of various Departments shall be maintained in respect of various cadres of the following Departments, offices, shops and sections: 

 13. Respondent Nos. 1 and 2 have challenged the legality of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 contending that prior to the making of the said order and that giving effect thereto the Corporation used to maintain combined seniority list of the personnel of Pay Group IV of the 3 shops, viz. Mechanical, Electrical and Bench Fitting of the GSE Department and that promotion to the post of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V used to be made from the personnel of Pay Group IV on the basis of combined seniority but by the Organisation Order 13 of 1995 existing practice of combined seniority list of the personnel in Pay Group IV has been abolished and that provision has been made for preparation of separate seniority list of the personnel of the 3, shops mentioned herein above and to make promotion to the posts of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V on the basis of said separate list and that thereby junior personnel of other shops would be promoted to the post of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V to the exclusion or deprivation of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 who are personnel of Bench Fitting of GSE Department. It was also the contention of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 that their secured/vested right of being promoted to Pay Group V in the posts of Junior Officers' Maintenance on the basis of combined seniority has been violated and consequent thereupon they have been deprived of their right of being promoted in Pay Group V and, as such, Organisation Order 13 of 1995 being discriminatory as well as violative of fundamental right guaranteed in the Constitution, the same is not legal. 

 15. Regulation 15 of the Regulations provides for maintenance of seniority list of the personnel of the Corporation. From the provision of the said Regulation, as is inside the bracket at the bottom, it is seen that the Corporation is required to maintain Cadre-wise separate seniority list for different shops and that within the shops cadre- wise seniority list of each section. The case of the appellants is based on the provision as is inside the bracket at the bottom of Regulation 15, that is, the said provision requires the Corporation to maintain cadre-wise separate seniority list of the different shops and that of each section within the shops. In the course of hearing of the appeal the learned Counsel representing the appellants in Appeal No. 25 of 2000 placed before the Court a copy of draft seniority list, which is not disputed or challenged from the side of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in Appeal No. 25 of 2000, circulated by the memo ঢাকাজিএফ/জেষ্টতা তালিকা/৮৯/৩৩০ dated 2-2-1989 amongst personnel of GSE Department and therein seniority of the personnel of three shops namely, Mechanical, Electrical and Bench Fitting was shown category-wise separately. This fact shows that long before making of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 practice of maintaining separate seniority list of the 3 shops namely, Mechanical, Electrical, Bench Fitting of GSE Department was in existence and that being the position, respondent Nos. 1 and 2's case of promotion on the basis of combined seniority list from Pay Group IV to V is not supported either by the provision of the Regulations or by any material in the record. The position in law being that the Corporation is required to maintain separate list of seniority in view of the provision of Regulation 15 of the Regulations the High Court Division was in error in holding that the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were entitled to be promoted from Pay Group V to the post of Junior Officers Maintenance on the basis of combined seniority list but because of separate seniority list circulated on the making of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were deprived of their secured right of being promoted to Pay Group V and thereupon in declaring Organisation Order 13 of 1995 and the seniority list circulated by the Memo dated 30-12-1995 as not legal. 

 16. By the judgment under appeal the learned Judges of the High Court Division on the view that by Organisation Order 13 of 1995 provision for making separate seniority list of the 3 shops of GSE Department was made and thereby having had violated previously existing practice of combined seniority list of the personnel in Pay Group IV of the aforesaid 3 shops and consequent thereupon the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 were adversely affected as well as deprived of accrued right of being promoted to Pay Group V have declared that the said order was made without lawful authority and that have also further declared the separate seniority list of the said 3 shops circulated by the memo dated 30-12-1995 not legal and that promotion of appellant in Appeal No. 26 of 2000 (respondent Nos. 5 and 6 in the writ petition) was illegal. As it has already been seen hereinbefore that at no time before making of Organisational Order 13 of 1995 there was practice of maintaining combined seniority list of the 3 shops i.e. Mechanical, Electrical and Bench Fitting of GSE Department, rather the Regulations required the Corporation to maintain separate seniority list of personnel of different shops and of the Section within the shops. That being the position in law the learned Judges of the High Court Division was in error, although found that Director Administration by virtue of delegation of power was competent to make Organisation Order 13 of 1995, in declaring the Organisation Order 13 of 1995 on the ground of making provision for preparation of separate seniority list of the personnel of the 3 shops and that the seniority list circulated under Memo dated 30-12-1995 on the ground of adversely affecting seniority of the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and that declaring the promotion of appellants in Appeal No. 26 of 2000 illegal on the ground of promoting them on the basis of separate seniority list to the posts of Junior Officer Maintenance in Pay Group V. 

 18. The learned Counsel for the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in Appeal No. 25 of 2000 in support of his contention that Organisation Order 13 of 1995 and the separate seniority list circulated by the memo dated 30-12-1995 were illegal, without jurisdiction and void being violative of the existing or that accrued secured right of the respondents prior to making of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 and circulation of separate seniority list of the 3 shops by the memo dated 30-12-1995 for being promoted to the post of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V on the basis of combined seniority has referred to the decision AIR 1982 (SC) 1064. In the reported case it has been observed: "Even otherwise, when a statutory rule governing seniority is issued in respect of a service, the said rule would govern the personnel in the service with effect from the date of its promulgation and in so giving effect to the rule in future, there is no element of retroactivity involved. Of course, the rules will not operate to deprive any person of promotions already earned in the past. 

 19. Since in the present case there in no question of depriving the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of their earned right of promotion, so the decision referred is not one relevant to the point involved in the instant case. The Corporation by Organisation Order 13 of 1995 has not introduced separate seniority list of the different shops of GSE Department, rather it is seen from the papers placed before this court that maintaining of separate seniority list of the personnel of three shops of GSE was in existence from before Organisation Order 13 of 1995, and that as in no way Organisation Order 13 of 1995 has divested the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of their any accrued or earned right in any respect, the said order cannot be considered illegal or void on the ground of depriving the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 of their right of being promoted to Pay Group V or that on the ground of adversely affecting the said respondents as to their right of promotion on the basis of supposed combined seniority list. 

 20. The other decision referred to reported in AIR 1993 (SC) 978 is also of no assistance to the learned Advocate representing the respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in any respect, not to speak of, adding force to the contention as to illegality of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 and the separate seniority list, since in the instant case no question of discrimination or that of violation of any kind of fundamental right granted in the Constitution is involved. 

 21. The facts of the aforesaid two cases are quite distinct and different from the facts of the instant case in that in the instant case it has already been found that there was no practice of maintaining combined seniority list of the personnel of Pay Group IV of different shops in GSE Department and the sections therein, rather Regulation 15 of the Regulations provides for preparation of separate seniority list of the personnel of different shops and the section therein. 

 22. Regulation 12(1) of the Regulations does in no way show that promotion of the personnel of the Corporation to the higher posts is a vested right. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 in Appeal No. 25 of 2000 who are the personnel of Bench Fitting shop of GSE Department at no point of time earned any right of being promoted to Pay Group V on the basis of non-existent combined seniority list nor they had any vested right at any time before making of Organisation Order 13 of 1995 and circulation of separate seniority list by the memo dated 30-12-1995 of being promoted to the post of Junior Officers Maintenance in Pay Group V and, as such, they have riot been deprived of any guaranteed right or discriminated. That being the position the contention of violation of provisions in Articles 27, 29 and 31 of the Constitution is not a well founded one.
